t: This is the bronze statue of John Cartwright, made by the sculptor George Clarke and put up in 1831, several years after Cartwright's death. It stands near his former home on Burton Crescent, and it has been listed since 1974. Cartwright is known as the Father of Reform. He served in the Royal Navy until the American Revolutionary War, left because he supported the colonies' self-determination, and then spent decades pressing for changes in Parliament, including universal suffrage and equal representation. He also argued for the abolition of slavery.
